title: Make the task-sync refusal-path test derive its expected path from the product's canonicalization and print stderr on failure
outcome: Make the task-sync refusal-path test derive its expected path from the product's canonicalization and print stderr on failure
acceptance: boundaries::task_sync_json_file_refusal_omits_the_plain_reading_path_context derives its expected reading path through the same canonicalization the product uses for the data checkout, so it passes on Windows whether the test root is spelled canonically or not (different case, 8.3 short name, junction or subst).
On failure the assertion message includes the actual stderr of the refused command.

Passes on Windows from a root whose spelling differs from its canonical form, and on Linux and macOS; no product rendering change unless the investigation shows the product prints a non-canonical or \\?\-prefixed path to users.
